candidates.attacker_control: The redirect target is taken from an ordinary HTTP request parameter: 'redirectUrl' (POST to /dso-display) and 'callerUrl' (GET or POST to /controlledvocabulary). No authentication or object-level authorization is required for either servlet: web.xml maps them at /dso-display and /controlledvocabulary, and the only filter mappings are admin-only for /dspace-admin/* and registered-only for /mydspace, /tools/*, /profile, /submit, /subscribe, /workspace, /view-workspaceitem (web.xml lines 84-127), so both endpoints are reachable anonymously. A crafted link (or a cross-site auto-submitted form for the POST-only /dso-display) makes the server emit a 302 Location header pointing at an arbitrary absolute URL.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that no security constraint/filter covers the two URL patterns (web.xml lines 79-127 vs. servlet mappings 769-772 and 794-797). Checked that other redirect sites in the same module (HandleServlet line 781, MyDSpaceServlet lines 195/210/492, OpenURLServlet lines 68-70, Authenticate line 127) build paths from request.getContextPath() or internal values, so the two servlets are outliers. Checked that the redirect targets are not re-validated later (no allow-list helper exists in the module; grep for startsWith(request.getContextPath()) returns nothing). Checked that Tomcat's sendRedirect will forward an absolute external URL; container-level header validation does not restrict Location to the same host. Counter-consideration: open redirects are often rated lower impact than XSS/RCE, and DSpace's servlet container may be fronted by a proxy that could (but by default does not) normalize Location headers.
candidates.impact: Open redirect on the trusted repository origin. This is usable for phishing/credential-harvesting chains ('verify your DSpace account' links that really point off-site), for bypassing trusted-domain allow lists in downstream consumers of DSpace URLs, and for leaking referral/context information. Severity is moderate (integrity of user navigation, not code execution), but it is exploitable without any account and with no configuration assumptions.
candidates.prerequisites: None for /controlledvocabulary (a simple GET with ?callerUrl=https://attacker.example/ works). For /dso-display the request must be a POST, which an attacker can trigger cross-site with an auto-submitting form; the JSPUI normally posts this form from search/results.jsp (hidden field redirectUrl) via static/js/search-results.js. Victim interaction (clicking the link/submitting the form) is required. No runtime test was executed.
candidates.root_cause: User-supplied request parameters are used directly as the target of HttpServletResponse.sendRedirect with no same-origin/allow-list/scheme-host validation (and no use of the context path, unlike the other redirects in the same module, which all prefix request.getContextPath()). In SearchResultLogServlet the parameter is 'redirectUrl' (read at line 40, sink at line 71); in ControlledVocabularyServlet the parameter is 'callerUrl' (read at line 38, sink at line 53).
candidates.title: Unauthenticated open redirect via unvalidated redirect parameters in JSPUI servlets (SearchResultLogServlet and ControlledVocabularyServlet)
candidates.trace: GET /controlledvocabulary?callerUrl=https://attacker.example/ -> ControlledVocabularyServlet.doDSGet (line 38 stores raw parameter) -> response.sendRedirect(callerUrl) (line 53) -> 302 Location: https://attacker.example/. POST /dso-display with redirectUrl=https://attacker.example/ -> SearchResultLogServlet.doDSPost (line 40 stores raw parameter; used at line 43 only for statistics handle extraction) -> response.sendRedirect(redirectUrl) (line 71) -> 302 Location: https://attacker.example/. Nothing between read and sink constrains the value: the surrounding statistics logic does not validate it, and encodeRedirectURL (used elsewhere in the codebase) would not make it same-origin anyway.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; no deployment/proxy configuration was inspected (a reverse proxy could in principle rewrite Location headers). Cannot confirm from source whether a later DSpace security release patched exactly these lines (no git history or patches available in this run). The second location (ControlledVocabularyServlet) is the same root cause and pattern, but only one of the two may correspond to any given historical fix.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 2286 model-visible files, no over-5MiB exclusions, no sensitive-name/path exclusions, no symlink exclusions (binary files skipped). Spot-reviewed: JSPUI servlets/filters/web.xml/JSPs (SearchResultLogServlet, ControlledVocabularyServlet, BitstreamServlet, RetrieveServlet, HTMLServlet, HandleServlet, FeedbackServlet, FeedServlet, OpenSearchServlet, OpenURLServlet, JSONServlet, SuggestServlet, RequestItemServlet, ItemMapServlet, DSpaceServlet, Authenticate, AbstractBrowserServlet, JSPManager, browse/*.jsp, search/*.jsp, tools/itemmap-browse.jsp, suggest/suggest.jsp), XMLUI aspects/readers/actions, dspace-api core (AuthorizeManager/ResourcePolicy, content Bitstream/Item/Bundle, browse engine, discovery/SolrServiceImpl, XML/XXE parsers, ItemImport, mediafilter exec sinks, OpenSearch/SyndicationFeed, Email), dspace-oai (controller, filters), dspace-rest resources, dspace-sword and dspace-swordv2 URL handling, dspace-lni DAV parsers, dspace-rdf negotiation, bundled Solr solrconfig.xml files, and top-level/web.xml/filter configuration. This was targeted breadth-first sampling and trace-following, not a line-by-line audit of all 2286 files; test sources are not present in the snapshot.
limitations: No execution, build, scanner, or runtime confirmation was performed; all conclusions are source-reading only.

No git history, upstream diff, patch, CVE/CWE label, or precomputed source-relation index is available in this run, so the assignment of the finding to any particular historical security fix/CVE could not be verified.
Container/proxy behavior (e.g. Location-header rewriting or host allow-lists) depends on deployment configuration not present in the snapshot.

Only the source files exposed by the tools could be inspected; generated code, dependency jars, and binary assets are out of scope, and large sections of the 2286-file tree (e.g. many XMLUI aspects, statistics/usage logging, workflow internals) were sampled rather than exhaustively read.

Several alternative candidate classes (XSS sinks, XXE-capable parsers, Solr remote streaming) remain unconfirmed; they were deliberately not submitted because the one-candidate cap was used for the strongest, most directly evidenced issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in JSPUI /tools/itemmap ('query' parameter concatenated into 'browsetext' in DiscoverySearchRequestProcessor.doItemMapSearch line 563 and printed unescaped as a fmt:param in dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/tools/itemmap-browse.jsp lines 58/62)
rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking missing output encoding and no result set needed, but ItemMapServlet.doDSPost first calls AuthorizeManager.authorizeAction(context, collection, COLLECTION_ADMIN) (ItemMapServlet.java lines 91-95), so exploitation requires a collection administrator account; kept out of the top candidate as a higher-prerequisite, unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: XSS in JSPUI browse full page: request 'value' flows through AbstractBrowserServlet (line 88/282) -> BrowseEngine -> BrowseInfo.setValue and is printed unescaped in dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/browse/full.jsp line 180 and hidden inputs lines 199/279, while the analogous single.jsp output is escaped with Utils.addEntities (line 278)
rejected_leads.reason: Strong inconsistency, but the browse engine applies an exact-match filter (scope.setFilterValue + filterValuePartial=false) and only renders full.jsp when results exist, so an attacker-chosen payload normally requires the value to first exist in indexed metadata (e.g. via an item submission). Not assumption-free, so not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: XSS via 'did you mean' spellcheck: dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/search/discovery.jsp line 199 prints spellCheckQuery unescaped in the anchor body (only the data-spell attribute is escaped), with spellCheckQuery coming from Solr spellcheck collation in SolrServiceImpl lines 1936-1943
rejected_leads.reason: Reachability depends on Solr spellcheck being enabled and on the collation echoing attacker-controlled characters; could not verify the Solr tokenizer/collation behavior from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored XSS in dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/suggest/suggest.jsp line 85 where an item's dc.title is printed unescaped while the other form fields use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml; page is reached through /suggest (public) after a Referer check
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a malicious item title (submission rights) plus a same-host Referer; plausible but weaker and unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsers without XXE hardening in request-processing paths (e.g. dspace-lni DAVResource.java SAXBuilder parses of request bodies at lines 607/860/1209/1678/1770; RoleIngester, ItemImport, ItemArchive, RegistryLoader DocumentBuilderFactory instances without FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING/disallow-doctype-decl)
rejected_leads.reason: Mostly reached by administrative commands/ingests; the LNI webapp is optional and not part of the default deployment, so prerequisites and exposure are unclear.

rejected_leads.lead: Bundled Solr configs enable remote streaming: dspace/solr/*/conf/solrconfig.xml (e.g. authority lock line 584, oai/search/statistics line 719) set enableRemoteStreaming="true" while the /solr webapp is deployed alongside DSpace
rejected_leads.reason: Deployment/hardening issue (SSRF/local file read via stream.url/stream.file if /solr is exposed without authentication) rather than a single code-level defect; network exposure is configuration-dependent and the config file itself warns about authentication.

rejected_leads.lead: OpenURLServlet / OpenURLReader build a Location value from unencoded 'title'/'aufirst'/'aulast' parameters (dspace-jspui OpenURLServlet lines 38-70, xmlui OpenURLReader lines 106-135)
rejected_leads.reason: Target remains the local simple-search path (no external host), and modern containers reject CR/LF in header values, so no concrete open redirect or response-splitting impact could be established from source.

summary: Snapshot is the JSPUI/XMLUI web application DSpace 5.10 (all module POMs declare 5.10; 5.x TableRow/DAO architecture, JSPUI, XMLUI, OAI, REST, SWORD, RDF, LNI, bundled Solr). Reviewed web-facing entry points, servlet filters, redirect/URL handling, JSP output encoding, XML parsers and bundled Solr configuration. The single strongest, assumption-free issue is an unauthenticated open redirect in the JSPUI: request parameters are passed verbatim to HttpServletResponse.sendRedirect in two publicly reachable servlets (SearchResultLogServlet mounted at /dso-display and ControlledVocabularyServlet mounted at /controlledvocabulary). Neither URL is covered by the admin-only or registered-only filter mappings, and neither servlet performs any validation that the redirect target is local. Other reviewed leads (several possible XSS sinks, XXE-capable parsers, Solr remote streaming) are noted as unconfirmed/rejected because each requires additional preconditions or assumptions.
